summary:
SpaceTrace AI is an interactive, AI-powered space exploration platform designed to bring the forgotten stories of spacecraft, rovers, landers, and scientific equipment left on the Moon and Mars to life, especially for young learners.

Developed for NASA's “Abandoned but Not Forgotten” challenge, our platform transforms complex NASA mission information into engaging, age-appropriate learning experiences through immersive 3D exploration, interactive storytelling, quizzes, and educational activities.

At the heart of SpaceTrace AI is **Ask Astro**, an intelligent AI assistant that helps children explore space history through natural-language questions. By combining NASA mission references with AI-assisted explanations, the platform makes scientific knowledge easier to understand while providing supporting sources.

Built using React, Three.js, ASP.NET Core, and Azure cloud technologies, SpaceTrace AI connects modern technology with the history of space exploration.

**Our mission is simple: A spacecraft's journey may end, but its story should never be forgotten.** By inspiring curiosity and making space science accessible, SpaceTrace AI encourages the next generation of scientists, engineers, and astronauts to explore beyond the stars.
details:
SpaceTrace AI – Bringing Forgotten Space Missions to Life

Project Overview

SpaceTrace AI is an innovative, AI-powered educational platform developed for NASA's “Abandoned but Not Forgotten” challenge. Our project brings the untold stories of spacecraft, rovers, landers, and scientific instruments left behind on the Moon and Mars to life through immersive 3D exploration, interactive storytelling, and artificial intelligence.

Our goal is to transform complex space science into an exciting, accessible, and engaging learning experience, particularly for children and young space enthusiasts.

How Does It Work?

SpaceTrace AI combines interactive visualization, NASA mission information, and AI-assisted learning to create a personalized space exploration experience.

  • Immersive 3D Exploration: Users can navigate an interactive space environment and discover spacecraft and equipment associated with historical missions.
  • AI-Powered Space Assistant – Ask Astro: Children can ask natural-language questions about spacecraft, mission discoveries, and why missions ended. The assistant uses relevant NASA references to support informative, age-appropriate explanations.
  • Interactive Mission Stories: Users can explore the history, purpose, scientific achievements, and legacy of individual space missions.
  • Personalized Learning: Junior and Explorer modes help make scientific information understandable for different learning levels.
  • Gamified Education: Interactive quizzes, exploration activities, and a digital explorer passport encourage curiosity and active participation.
  • NASA-Referenced Knowledge: Mission information and supporting source links help users connect AI-assisted explanations with credible scientific resources.

Benefits and Intended Impact

SpaceTrace AI addresses an important educational challenge: scientific mission information is often technical, fragmented across multiple sources, and difficult for younger audiences to understand.

Our platform makes space exploration more accessible by combining visual learning, interactive experiences, and conversational AI.

The intended benefits include:

  • Inspiring children to develop an interest in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM).
  • Making NASA's space exploration history engaging and easier to understand.
  • Encouraging independent learning through questions and discovery.
  • Preserving awareness of the scientific contributions of completed space missions.
  • Demonstrating how artificial intelligence can support interactive education.

We envision SpaceTrace AI becoming a digital learning companion that connects the next generation of explorers with the remarkable achievements of past space missions.

Technologies and Tools Used

We developed SpaceTrace AI using a modern full-stack architecture.

Frontend Technologies:

  • React and TypeScript for the interactive application.
  • Three.js and React Three Fiber for immersive 3D visualization.
  • Vite for frontend development and application building.
  • Responsive web design for an engaging experience across devices.

Backend Technologies:

  • C# and ASP.NET Core (.NET 10) for backend services.
  • REST APIs for communication between the frontend and backend.
  • Mission discovery, exploration, and AI question-answering endpoints.

Artificial Intelligence and Cloud:

  • Azure OpenAI integration support for AI-assisted storytelling and conversational question answering.
  • NASA Science mission references and imagery resources for factual content.
  • Microsoft Azure App Service for backend hosting.

The platform is web-based and does not require specialized hardware.

What Makes Our Project Creative?

The unique concept behind SpaceTrace AI is that spacecraft do not become unimportant when their missions end.

Instead of presenting space history as static scientific information, our platform turns abandoned and retired space equipment into the center of an interactive learning journey.

By combining immersive 3D environments, AI-assisted storytelling, and educational gamification, we encourage children to discover the fascinating stories behind these silent explorers.

Rather than simply reading about a spacecraft, a child can explore its mission, understand its achievements, and ask questions about its journey.

Our creativity lies in connecting historical scientific knowledge with modern AI technology to make learning feel like a space adventure.

Key Factors Considered During Development

Throughout development, our team focused on:

  1. Scientific Accuracy: Using NASA references to support mission information and AI-generated explanations.
  2. Child-Friendly Experience: Designing intuitive navigation, engaging visuals, and explanations suitable for younger learners.
  3. Accessibility: Building a responsive web application that can be used without specialized equipment.
  4. Interactive Learning: Encouraging exploration, curiosity, and critical thinking rather than passive reading.
  5. Responsible AI: Supporting source-based answers and appropriate fallback behavior when AI services or sufficient evidence are unavailable.
  6. Scalability: Using a modular frontend and backend architecture that can support additional missions and learning features in the future.

Conclusion

SpaceTrace AI is more than a space exploration application. It is a bridge between NASA's extraordinary scientific achievements and the curiosity of future generations.

We believe that even when a spacecraft stops functioning, its discoveries, contributions, and legacy deserve to continue inspiring people.

Our vision is simple: Every mission leaves a story, and every story can inspire the next explorer.

Through the power of AI, interactive technology, and NASA's scientific knowledge, SpaceTrace AI ensures that the explorers humanity left behind are never forgotten.
